title: KVzap: Fast, Adaptive, and Faithful KV Cache Pruning
one_line_claim: Lightweight surrogate models approximate expensive KV cache scoring, enabling 2-4x compression with negligible accuracy loss across long-context and reasoning tasks.
method_summary: KVzap trains lightweight linear or MLP models to approximate KVzip+ scores (computed via copy-paste pretext tasks) for token importance ranking. At inference, tokens below an adaptive threshold are evicted. Operates in a prefix-agnostic manner during both prefilling and decoding phases.

key_findings.finding: Achieves 2-4x KV cache compression with negligible accuracy loss.
key_findings.quote: 2-4x KV cache compression with negligible accuracy loss

key_findings.finding: State-of-the-art on RULER long-context benchmark, outperforming KVzip+ and other pruning methods.
key_findings.quote: State-of-the-art results on RULER, a challenging long-context benchmark spanning sequences up to 1M tokens

key_findings.finding: Adaptive threshold mechanism adjusts compression dynamically across layers and generation phases.
key_findings.quote: Adaptive compression rates can be achieved through dynamic threshold adjustment across layers and generation phases

relation_to_herald.shared: Both operate on per-token signals without full forward-backward passes and aim to improve efficiency of long-context inference.
differs_on: KVzap predicts token importance for pruning decisions; HERALD predicts catastrophic failure onset from logit signals.
KVzap mitigates compression-induced degradation through selective eviction; HERALD detects when degradation occurs and enables intervention.
KVzap operates deterministically via thresholding; HERALD uses probabilistic XGBoost scores with a horizon parameter.
